about: Oracle Database 23ai SQL and PL/SQL vocabulary, merged over common.json. Also used for Db2, Teradata, Informix and SAP HANA connections.

functions.name: LISTAGG
functions.summary: Concatenates the values of a column into one string, separated by a delimiter and ordered by WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...). Also usable as an analytic function with OVER.

params.name: [ALL | DISTINCT] measure_expr
params.doc: The value to concatenate; NULLs are skipped. DISTINCT removes duplicate values first.

params.name: delimiter [ON OVERFLOW ...]
params.doc: Text placed between values (none by default). Follow with ON OVERFLOW TRUNCATE ['...'] [WITH | WITHOUT COUNT] or ON OVERFLOW ERROR to control over-long results.

functions.name: COLLECT
functions.summary: Gathers the values of a column into a nested table. Usually wrapped in CAST to a named collection type.

params.name: [DISTINCT | UNIQUE] column [ORDER BY expr]
params.doc: The value to collect; DISTINCT drops duplicates and ORDER BY sets the element order.

functions.name: MEDIAN
functions.summary: Returns the middle value (interpolated between the two middle values when needed) of a numeric or datetime expression, ignoring NULLs.
functions.example: SELECT department_id, MEDIAN(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY department_id

params.name: expr
params.doc: The value whose median is computed.

functions.name: STDDEV
functions.summary: Returns the sample standard deviation of an expression. Unlike STDDEV_SAMP it returns 0, not NULL, for a single row.

params.name: [DISTINCT | ALL] expr
params.doc: The numeric value; DISTINCT considers each value once.

functions.name: STDDEV_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population standard deviation of an expression (the square root of VAR_POP).

functions.name: STDDEV_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the cumulative sample standard deviation of an expression (the square root of VAR_SAMP). Returns NULL for a single row.

functions.name: VARIANCE
functions.summary: Returns the sample variance of an expression. Unlike VAR_SAMP it returns 0, not NULL, for a single row.

params.name: [DISTINCT | ALL] expr
params.doc: The numeric value; DISTINCT considers each value once.

functions.name: VAR_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population variance of a set of numbers after discarding NULLs.

functions.name: VAR_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the sample variance of a set of numbers after discarding NULLs. Returns NULL for a single row.

functions.name: CORR
functions.summary: Returns the Pearson correlation coefficient of a set of number pairs, ignoring pairs where either value is NULL.

params.name: expr1
params.doc: The first numeric value of each pair.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The second numeric value of each pair.

functions.name: CORR_S
functions.summary: Returns Spearman's rho rank correlation coefficient of a set of number pairs.

params.name: expr1
params.doc: The first numeric value of each pair.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The second numeric value of each pair.

functions.name: CORR_K
functions.summary: Returns Kendall's tau-b rank correlation coefficient of a set of number pairs.

params.name: expr1
params.doc: The first numeric value of each pair.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The second numeric value of each pair.

functions.name: COVAR_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population covariance of a set of number pairs.

params.name: expr1
params.doc: The first numeric value of each pair.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The second numeric value of each pair.

functions.name: COVAR_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the sample covariance of a set of number pairs.

params.name: expr1
params.doc: The first numeric value of each pair.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The second numeric value of each pair.

functions.name: REGR_SLOPE
functions.summary: Returns the slope of the least-squares regression line fitted to non-NULL (y, x) pairs.

functions.name: REGR_INTERCEPT
functions.summary: Returns the y-intercept of the least-squares regression line fitted to non-NULL (y, x) pairs.

functions.name: REGR_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns the number of non-NULL (y, x) pairs used to fit the regression line.

functions.name: REGR_R2
functions.summary: Returns the coefficient of determination (R squared) of the regression line.

functions.name: REGR_AVGX
functions.summary: Returns the average of the independent variable x over non-NULL (y, x) pairs.

functions.name: REGR_AVGY
functions.summary: Returns the average of the dependent variable y over non-NULL (y, x) pairs.

functions.name: REGR_SXX
functions.summary: Returns REGR_COUNT * VAR_POP(x), an auxiliary regression statistic.

functions.name: REGR_SYY
functions.summary: Returns REGR_COUNT * VAR_POP(y), an auxiliary regression statistic.

functions.name: REGR_SXY
functions.summary: Returns REGR_COUNT * COVAR_POP(y, x), an auxiliary regression statistic.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT
functions.summary: Returns an approximate count of distinct non-NULL values, much faster than COUNT(DISTINCT expr) on large data.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The value whose distinct count is estimated.

functions.name: APPROX_MEDIAN
functions.summary: Returns an approximate median of a numeric or datetime expression, or its error rate or confidence.

params.name: expr [DETERMINISTIC]
params.doc: The value whose median is estimated; DETERMINISTIC gives repeatable results.

params.name: info
params.doc: 'ERROR_RATE' or 'CONFIDENCE' to return that statistic instead of the median.

functions.name: APPROX_PERCENTILE
functions.summary: Returns an approximate percentile of the ordered values, like a faster PERCENTILE_DISC.

params.name: percentile [DETERMINISTIC]
params.doc: A percentile between 0 and 1; DETERMINISTIC gives repeatable results.

params.name: info
params.doc: 'ERROR_RATE' or 'CONFIDENCE' to return that statistic instead.

functions.name: APPROX_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns an approximate count of an expression; used with APPROX_RANK to find top-N groups quickly.
functions.example: SELECT job_id, APPROX_COUNT(*) FROM employees GROUP BY job_id

params.name: 'MAX_ERROR'
params.doc: Pass 'MAX_ERROR' to return the maximum error instead of the count.

functions.name: APPROX_SUM
functions.summary: Returns an approximate sum of an expression; used with APPROX_RANK to find top-N groups quickly.
functions.example: SELECT job_id, APPROX_SUM(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY job_id

params.name: 'MAX_ERROR'
params.doc: Pass 'MAX_ERROR' to return the maximum error instead of the sum.

functions.name: PERCENTILE_CONT
functions.summary: Returns the value at a percentile of the ordered values, interpolating between neighbours (continuous distribution). Also usable with OVER.

params.name: percentile
params.doc: A percentile between 0 and 1. The values come from WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expr).

functions.name: PERCENTILE_DISC
functions.summary: Returns the first value whose cumulative distribution reaches a percentile of the ordered values (discrete distribution). Also usable with OVER.

params.name: percentile
params.doc: A percentile between 0 and 1. The values come from WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expr).

functions.name: JSON_ARRAYAGG
functions.summary: Aggregates values into a JSON array, one element per row.
functions.example: SELECT JSON_ARRAYAGG(last_name ORDER BY last_name) FROM employees

params.name: expr [FORMAT JSON] [ORDER BY ...] [NULL | ABSENT ON NULL] [RETURNING data_type] [STRICT]
params.doc: The element value, optionally ordered; NULLs are omitted unless NULL ON NULL is given.

functions.name: JSON_OBJECTAGG
functions.summary: Aggregates key/value pairs from each row into one JSON object.
functions.example: SELECT JSON_OBJECTAGG(KEY department_name VALUE department_id) FROM departments

params.name: [KEY] key_expr VALUE value_expr [NULL | ABSENT ON NULL] [RETURNING data_type] [WITH UNIQUE KEYS]
params.doc: The member name and value for each row; the name must be a string. A colon may replace VALUE.

functions.name: JSON_DATAGUIDE
functions.summary: Aggregates JSON documents into a data guide describing their structure (paths and types).

params.name: flag
params.doc: Options such as DBMS_JSON.PRETTY or DBMS_JSON.GEOJSON.

functions.name: XMLAGG
functions.summary: Aggregates XML fragments from each row into one XML value.
functions.example: SELECT XMLAGG(XMLELEMENT("name", last_name) ORDER BY last_name) FROM employees

params.name: XMLType_instance [ORDER BY ...]
params.doc: The XML fragment to aggregate; NULLs are dropped. ORDER BY sets the fragment order.

functions.name: ANY_VALUE
functions.summary: Returns a single non-deterministic value of an expression from each group, avoiding GROUP BY on columns that are constant per group.
functions.example: SELECT department_id, ANY_VALUE(department_name) FROM employees JOIN departments USING (department_id) GROUP BY department_id

params.name: [DISTINCT | ALL] expr
params.doc: The value to return; DISTINCT and ALL are accepted but have no effect.

functions.name: GROUPING
functions.summary: Returns 1 when a row is a superaggregate row produced by ROLLUP, CUBE or GROUPING SETS for that column, else 0.
functions.example: SELECT department_id, GROUPING(department_id), SUM(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY ROLLUP(department_id)

params.name: expr
params.doc: An expression from the GROUP BY clause.

functions.name: GROUPING_ID
functions.summary: Returns a number whose bits are the GROUPING values of the listed columns, identifying the grouping level of each row.

params.name: expr
params.doc: An expression from the GROUP BY clause; one bit per expression.

functions.name: GROUP_ID
functions.summary: Distinguishes duplicate groups produced by a GROUP BY: returns 0 for the first copy and n for the nth duplicate.
functions.example: SELECT GROUP_ID(), SUM(amount) FROM sales GROUP BY ROLLUP(region, region)

functions.name: STATS_MODE
functions.summary: Returns the value that occurs most often in a set; when several tie, one of them is returned.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The value whose mode is found.

functions.name: BIT_AND_AGG
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise AND of all non-NULL integer values in each group. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: BIT_OR_AGG
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise OR of all non-NULL integer values in each group. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: BIT_XOR_AGG
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise XOR of all non-NULL integer values in each group. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: CHECKSUM
functions.summary: Computes an order-independent checksum over the values of an expression, useful to detect changes in a table. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: KURTOSIS_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population kurtosis (peakedness) of a set of numbers. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: KURTOSIS_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the sample kurtosis (peakedness) of a set of numbers. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: SKEWNESS_POP
functions.summary: Returns the population skewness (asymmetry) of a set of numbers. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: SKEWNESS_SAMP
functions.summary: Returns the sample skewness (asymmetry) of a set of numbers. (Oracle 21c+)

functions.name: BOOLEAN_AND_AGG
functions.summary: Returns TRUE when every non-NULL BOOLEAN value in the group is TRUE, else FALSE. (Oracle 23ai+)

functions.name: BOOLEAN_OR_AGG
functions.summary: Returns TRUE when any non-NULL BOOLEAN value in the group is TRUE, else FALSE. (Oracle 23ai+)

functions.name: RANK
functions.summary: Analytic: ranks each row within its partition, leaving gaps after ties. Aggregate: returns the rank a hypothetical row would have, with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...).
functions.example: RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC)

params.name: expr
params.doc: A hypothetical value; each matches one ORDER BY expression in WITHIN GROUP.

functions.name: DENSE_RANK
functions.summary: Analytic: ranks each row within its partition with no gaps after ties. Aggregate: returns the dense rank of a hypothetical row, with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...).

params.name: expr
params.doc: A hypothetical value; each matches one ORDER BY expression in WITHIN GROUP.

functions.name: PERCENT_RANK
functions.summary: Analytic: returns (rank - 1) / (rows in partition - 1), from 0 to 1. Aggregate: the percent rank of a hypothetical row, with WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY ...).
functions.example: PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary)

params.name: expr
params.doc: A hypothetical value; each matches one ORDER BY expression in WITHIN GROUP.

functions.name: CUME_DIST
functions.summary: Analytic: returns the fraction of rows in the partition ordered at or before the current row (0 to 1]. Aggregate: the cumulative distribution of a hypothetical row.
functions.example: CUME_DIST() OVER (PARTITION BY job_id ORDER BY salary)

params.name: expr
params.doc: A hypothetical value; each matches one ORDER BY expression in WITHIN GROUP.

functions.name: NTH_VALUE
functions.summary: Returns the value of an expression at the nth row of the window frame. Add FROM FIRST or FROM LAST and RESPECT or IGNORE NULLS after the parentheses.
functions.example: NTH_VALUE(salary, 2) FROM FIRST IGNORE NULLS OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC)

params.name: n
params.doc: Which row of the frame, counting from 1.

functions.name: RATIO_TO_REPORT
functions.summary: Returns the ratio of a value to the sum of that value over the partition.

params.name: expr
params.doc: The numeric value; NULL yields NULL.

functions.name: LENGTH
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in characters. An empty string is NULL in Oracle, so LENGTH('') is NULL.

params.name: char
params.doc: The string or LOB to measure.

functions.name: LENGTHB
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in bytes.

functions.name: LENGTHC
functions.summary: Returns the length of a string in Unicode complete characters.

functions.name: SUBSTR
functions.summary: Returns part of a string, starting at a character position. A negative position counts back from the end; 0 is treated as 1.

params.name: position
params.doc: Starting character position; negative counts from the end.

params.name: substring_length
params.doc: Number of characters to return; omitted means to the end.

functions.name: SUBSTRB
functions.summary: Like SUBSTR, but positions and length are measured in bytes.

params.name: position
params.doc: Starting byte position; negative counts from the end.

params.name: substring_length
params.doc: Number of bytes to return; omitted means to the end.

functions.name: INSTR
functions.summary: Returns the character position of a substring within a string, or 0 when it is not found.

params.name: position
params.doc: Character position to start at (default 1); negative searches backward from the end.

functions.name: INSTRB
functions.summary: Like INSTR, but positions are measured in bytes.

params.name: position
params.doc: Byte position to start at (default 1); negative searches backward from the end.

functions.name: CONCAT
functions.summary: Concatenates exactly two strings. Nest calls or use the || operator for more. NULL arguments are treated as empty strings.

functions.name: LPAD
functions.summary: Pads a string on the left to a given length with a set of characters, or truncates it to that length.

params.name: n
params.doc: The display length of the result.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The padding characters (default a single blank).

functions.name: RPAD
functions.summary: Pads a string on the right to a given length with a set of characters, or truncates it to that length.

params.name: n
params.doc: The display length of the result.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The padding characters (default a single blank).

functions.name: LTRIM
functions.summary: Removes from the left of a string every character that appears in a set (blanks by default).

params.name: set
params.doc: The characters to remove; default is a single blank.

functions.name: RTRIM
functions.summary: Removes from the right of a string every character that appears in a set (blanks by default).

params.name: set
params.doc: The characters to remove; default is a single blank.

functions.name: TRIM
functions.summary: Removes leading, trailing or both leading and trailing occurrences of one character (blank by default) from a string.

params.name: [LEADING | TRAILING | BOTH] [trim_character FROM] trim_source
params.doc: Which end to trim (BOTH by default), the single character to remove, then FROM and the string.

functions.name: INITCAP
functions.summary: Returns a string with the first letter of each word in uppercase and the rest in lowercase.

functions.name: REPLACE
functions.summary: Replaces every occurrence of a search string with a replacement string. With no replacement, the occurrences are removed.

params.name: replacement_string
params.doc: The text to put in its place; omitted or NULL removes the matches.

functions.name: TRANSLATE
functions.summary: Replaces each character in from_string with the character at the same position in to_string; characters with no counterpart are removed. TRANSLATE ... USING converts between database and national character sets.

params.name: to_string
params.doc: The replacement characters, matched by position.

params.name: char USING CHAR_CS | NCHAR_CS
params.doc: The text to convert, then USING and the target character set.

functions.name: REVERSE
functions.summary: Returns a string with its characters in reverse order. Works in SQL but is undocumented by Oracle; byte-based, so avoid it with multibyte data.

functions.name: ASCII
functions.summary: Returns the decimal code in the database character set of the first character of a string.

params.name: char
params.doc: The string whose first character is examined.

functions.name: CHR
functions.summary: Returns the character with the given code in the database character set, or in the national character set with USING NCHAR_CS.

params.name: n [USING NCHAR_CS]
params.doc: The character code; USING NCHAR_CS selects the national character set.

functions.name: NCHR
functions.summary: Returns the character with the given code in the national character set.

functions.name: SOUNDEX
functions.summary: Returns a four-character phonetic code of an English string, so similar-sounding words compare equal.

functions.name: REGEXP_LIKE
functions.summary: Condition that is true when a string matches a regular expression. Use in WHERE, or as a BOOLEAN value in 23ai.

params.name: match_param
params.doc: Matching options: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'n' dot matches newline, 'm' multiline, 'x' ignore whitespace.

functions.name: REGEXP_REPLACE
functions.summary: Replaces matches of a regular expression with a replacement string; \1 to \9 refer to captured groups.

params.name: replace_string
params.doc: The replacement text; omitted removes the matches.

params.name: occurrence
params.doc: Which match to replace; 0 (default) replaces all.

params.name: match_param
params.doc: Matching options: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'n' dot matches newline, 'm' multiline, 'x' ignore whitespace.

functions.name: REGEXP_SUBSTR
functions.summary: Returns the substring that matches a regular expression, or NULL when nothing matches.

params.name: match_param
params.doc: Matching options: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'n' dot matches newline, 'm' multiline, 'x' ignore whitespace.

params.name: subexpr
params.doc: Capture group to return, 1 to 9; 0 (default) returns the whole match.

functions.name: REGEXP_INSTR
functions.summary: Returns the position of a regular expression match in a string, or 0 when nothing matches.

params.name: return_opt
params.doc: 0 (default) returns the match start; 1 returns the position after the match.

params.name: match_param
params.doc: Matching options: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'n' dot matches newline, 'm' multiline, 'x' ignore whitespace.

params.name: subexpr
params.doc: Capture group whose position is returned; 0 (default) means the whole match.

functions.name: REGEXP_COUNT
functions.summary: Returns how many times a regular expression matches in a string.

params.name: match_param
params.doc: Matching options: 'i' case-insensitive, 'c' case-sensitive, 'n' dot matches newline, 'm' multiline, 'x' ignore whitespace.

functions.name: DUMP
functions.summary: Returns the internal representation of a value: its type code, length in bytes and each byte.

params.name: return_fmt
params.doc: 8 octal, 10 decimal (default), 16 hex, 17 characters; add 1000 to include the character set name.

functions.name: ASCIISTR
functions.summary: Returns an ASCII version of a string, with non-ASCII characters written as \xxxx UTF-16 escapes.

functions.name: UNISTR
functions.summary: Converts a string containing \xxxx Unicode escapes into national character set text.

functions.name: COMPOSE
functions.summary: Returns a string in Unicode NFC (fully normalized, composed) form.

functions.name: DECOMPOSE
functions.summary: Returns a Unicode string decomposed into base characters and combining marks.

functions.name: NLS_UPPER
functions.summary: Converts a string to uppercase using linguistic rules.

params.name: nlsparam
params.doc: Linguistic sort to use, such as 'NLS_SORT = XGerman'.

functions.name: NLS_LOWER
functions.summary: Converts a string to lowercase using linguistic rules.

params.name: nlsparam
params.doc: Linguistic sort to use, such as 'NLS_SORT = XGerman'.

functions.name: NLS_INITCAP
functions.summary: Capitalizes the first letter of each word using linguistic rules.

params.name: nlsparam
params.doc: Linguistic sort to use, such as 'NLS_SORT = XGerman'.

functions.name: NLSSORT
functions.summary: Returns the collation key of a string for a linguistic sort, for ordering or comparing text linguistically.

params.name: nlsparam
params.doc: Linguistic sort to use, such as 'NLS_SORT = XGerman'.

functions.name: CEIL
functions.summary: Returns the smallest integer greater than or equal to a number. In 23ai also rounds a date, timestamp or interval up to a unit.

params.name: fmt
params.doc: Unit to round up to, such as 'MM' or 'HH' (default 'DD').

functions.name: FLOOR
functions.summary: Returns the largest integer less than or equal to a number. In 23ai also rounds a date, timestamp or interval down to a unit.

params.name: fmt
params.doc: Unit to round down to, such as 'MM' or 'HH' (default 'DD').

functions.name: ROUND
functions.summary: Rounds a number to a number of decimal places, or a date to the nearest unit given by a format model (the nearest day by default).

params.name: integer
params.doc: Decimal places (default 0); negative rounds to the left of the point.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date, timestamp or (23ai) interval to round.

params.name: fmt
params.doc: Unit to round to, such as 'YYYY', 'MM', 'DD' or 'HH24' (default 'DD').

functions.name: TRUNC
functions.summary: Truncates a number to a number of decimal places, or a date to the unit given by a format model (midnight by default).

params.name: n2
params.doc: Decimal places to keep (default 0); negative zeroes digits left of the point.

params.name: date
params.doc: The date, timestamp or (23ai) interval to truncate.

params.name: fmt
params.doc: Unit to truncate to, such as 'YYYY', 'Q', 'MM', 'IW' or 'HH24' (default 'DD').

functions.name: MOD
functions.summary: Returns the remainder of n2 divided by n1, using FLOOR semantics for the sign; returns n2 when n1 is 0.

functions.name: REMAINDER
functions.summary: Returns the remainder of n2 divided by n1, using ROUND instead of FLOOR to compute the quotient.

functions.name: POWER
functions.summary: Returns n2 raised to the power n1.

params.name: n1
params.doc: The exponent; must be an integer when n2 is negative.

functions.name: SQRT
functions.summary: Returns the square root of a non-negative number.

functions.name: EXP
functions.summary: Returns e raised to the nth power.

functions.name: LN
functions.summary: Returns the natural logarithm of a number greater than 0.

functions.name: LOG
functions.summary: Returns the logarithm of n1 in base n2. Note the base comes first.

params.name: n1
params.doc: The number whose logarithm is returned; positive.

functions.name: SIGN
functions.summary: Returns -1, 0 or 1 for a negative, zero or positive number.

functions.name: SIN
functions.summary: Returns the sine of an angle in radians.

functions.name: COS
functions.summary: Returns the cosine of an angle in radians.

functions.name: TAN
functions.summary: Returns the tangent of an angle in radians.

functions.name: SINH
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic sine of a number.

functions.name: COSH
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of a number.

functions.name: TANH
functions.summary: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of a number.

functions.name: ASIN
functions.summary: Returns the arc sine of a number, in radians.

functions.name: ACOS
functions.summary: Returns the arc cosine of a number, in radians.

functions.name: ATAN
functions.summary: Returns the arc tangent of a number, in radians.

functions.name: ATAN2
functions.summary: Returns the arc tangent of n1/n2 in radians, using the signs of both to pick the quadrant.

functions.name: BITAND
functions.summary: Returns the bitwise AND of two integers.

functions.name: BIN_TO_NUM
functions.summary: Converts a list of bits (0 or 1) into the number they represent.

functions.name: WIDTH_BUCKET
functions.summary: Returns which of num_buckets equal-width buckets between min_value and max_value a value falls in; 0 below the range and num_buckets+1 above it.

functions.name: NANVL
functions.summary: Returns n1 when n2 is NaN, otherwise n2. Only meaningful for BINARY_FLOAT and BINARY_DOUBLE values.

params.name: n2
params.doc: The value to test for NaN.

params.name: n1
params.doc: The value to return instead of NaN.

functions.name: GREATEST
functions.summary: Returns the greatest of a list of expressions, compared using the type of the first. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: LEAST
functions.summary: Returns the least of a list of expressions, compared using the type of the first. Returns NULL if any argument is NULL.

functions.name: NVL
functions.summary: Returns expr2 when expr1 is NULL, otherwise expr1.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: The value returned when expr1 is NULL.

functions.name: NVL2
functions.summary: Returns expr2 when expr1 is not NULL, and expr3 when it is NULL.

params.name: expr2
params.doc: Returned when expr1 is not NULL.

functions.name: DECODE
functions.summary: Compares expr to each search value in turn and returns the matching result; returns the default (or NULL) when none match. Unlike =, DECODE treats two NULLs as equal.

params.name: search
params.doc: A value to compare expr with.

params.name: result
params.doc: Returned when expr equals the preceding search.

params.name: search | result | default
params.doc: More search/result pairs; a final unpaired argument is the default.

functions.name: LNNVL
functions.summary: Returns TRUE when a condition is FALSE or UNKNOWN, and FALSE when it is TRUE. Useful for NULL-safe negation in WHERE.

params.name: condition
params.doc: A simple condition on one or two scalar expressions.

functions.name: SYSDATE
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time of the database server's operating system, as a DATE (no fractional seconds or time zone).

functions.name: SYSTIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the database server's current date and time with fractional seconds and time zone.

functions.name: CURRENT_DATE
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time in the session time zone, as a DATE.

functions.name: CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time in the session time zone, with fractional seconds and time zone.

functions.name: LOCALTIMESTAMP
functions.summary: Returns the current date and time in the session time zone, without time zone information.

functions.name: SESSIONTIMEZONE
functions.summary: Returns the session time zone, as an offset such as '-05:00' or a region name.

functions.name: DBTIMEZONE
functions.summary: Returns the database time zone, as an offset such as '+00:00' or a region name.

functions.name: ADD_MONTHS
functions.summary: Adds a number of months to a date. If the date is the last day of its month, or the result month is shorter, the result is the last day of the month.

functions.name: MONTHS_BETWEEN
functions.summary: Returns the number of months between date1 and date2, positive when date1 is later. Fractional parts are based on a 31-day month.

params.name: date1
params.doc: The later date for a positive result.

functions.name: LAST_DAY
functions.summary: Returns the date of the last day of the month that contains a date, keeping its time of day.

functions.name: NEXT_DAY
functions.summary: Returns the date of the first named weekday that is later than a date.

params.name: char
params.doc: A day name or abbreviation in the session date language, such as 'MONDAY' or 'MON'.

keywords.name: MINUS
keywords.doc: Returns the distinct rows of the first query that are not returned by the second. Oracle's name for EXCEPT (EXCEPT is also accepted from 21c).
keywords.syntax: query MINUS [ALL] query

keywords.name: FETCH
keywords.doc: Limits the rows a query returns (row limiting clause), or in PL/SQL reads the next row(s) from a cursor.
keywords.syntax: FETCH { FIRST | NEXT } [n [PERCENT]] { ROW | ROWS } { ONLY | WITH TIES } | FETCH cursor INTO vars

keywords.name: FETCH FIRST
keywords.doc: Returns only the first n rows (or n percent) of the ordered result.
keywords.syntax: [OFFSET n ROWS] FETCH FIRST n ROWS { ONLY | WITH TIES }

keywords.name: FETCH NEXT
keywords.doc: Same as FETCH FIRST; reads naturally after OFFSET.
keywords.syntax: OFFSET n ROWS FETCH NEXT n ROWS ONLY

keywords.name: FIRST
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH FIRST, NULLS FIRST, KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST ...) and NTH_VALUE ... FROM FIRST.

keywords.name: LAST
keywords.doc: Used in NULLS LAST, KEEP (DENSE_RANK LAST ...) and NTH_VALUE ... FROM LAST.

keywords.name: NEXT
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH NEXT; synonym of FIRST there.

keywords.name: ONLY
keywords.doc: Ends a row limiting clause so exactly n rows are returned.
keywords.syntax: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY

keywords.name: ROWS ONLY
keywords.doc: Ends a row limiting clause so exactly n rows are returned.
keywords.syntax: FETCH FIRST n ROWS ONLY

keywords.name: WITH TIES
keywords.doc: Row limiting option that also returns rows tied with the last row on the ORDER BY key.
keywords.syntax: FETCH FIRST n ROWS WITH TIES

keywords.name: TIES
keywords.doc: Used in FETCH FIRST n ROWS WITH TIES.

keywords.name: PERCENT
keywords.doc: Makes a row limiting clause count a percentage of rows.
keywords.syntax: FETCH FIRST 10 PERCENT ROWS ONLY

keywords.name: OFFSET
keywords.doc: Skips a number of rows before the row limiting clause starts returning rows.
keywords.syntax: OFFSET n { ROW | ROWS } [FETCH ...]

keywords.name: CONNECT BY
keywords.doc: Defines the parent/child relationship of a hierarchical query; PRIOR marks the parent side.
keywords.syntax: [START WITH condition] CONNECT BY [NOCYCLE] PRIOR child_col = parent_col

keywords.name: CONNECT
keywords.doc: Used in CONNECT BY for hierarchical queries, and in GRANT CONNECT.

keywords.name: PRIOR
keywords.doc: In CONNECT BY, refers to the value in the parent row.
keywords.syntax: CONNECT BY PRIOR employee_id = manager_id

keywords.name: START WITH
keywords.doc: Specifies the root rows of a hierarchical query.
keywords.syntax: START WITH manager_id IS NULL CONNECT BY ...

keywords.name: START
keywords.doc: Used in START WITH (hierarchical queries) and sequence START WITH.

keywords.name: NOCYCLE
keywords.doc: Lets a CONNECT BY query return rows despite loops in the data; see CONNECT_BY_ISCYCLE.
keywords.syntax: CONNECT BY NOCYCLE PRIOR ...

keywords.name: LEVEL
keywords.doc: Pseudocolumn giving the depth of a row in a hierarchical query: 1 for a root, 2 for its children, and so on.
keywords.syntax: SELECT LEVEL, last_name FROM employees CONNECT BY PRIOR employee_id = manager_id

keywords.name: CONNECT_BY_ROOT
keywords.doc: Unary operator in a hierarchical query that returns a column's value from the root row of the current row's hierarchy.
keywords.syntax: CONNECT_BY_ROOT last_name

keywords.name: CONNECT_BY_ISLEAF
keywords.doc: Pseudocolumn that is 1 when the current row has no children in the hierarchy, else 0.

keywords.name: CONNECT_BY_ISCYCLE
keywords.doc: Pseudocolumn that is 1 when the current row has a child that is also its ancestor. Requires CONNECT BY NOCYCLE.

keywords.name: SIBLINGS
keywords.doc: Used in ORDER SIBLINGS BY to sort rows at each level of a hierarchy without breaking it.
keywords.syntax: ORDER SIBLINGS BY last_name

keywords.name: ORDER SIBLINGS BY
keywords.doc: Orders rows that share a parent in a hierarchical query, keeping the hierarchy intact.
keywords.syntax: ORDER SIBLINGS BY expr [ASC | DESC]

keywords.name: ROWNUM
keywords.doc: Pseudocolumn numbering rows as they are returned, starting at 1, before ORDER BY is applied. Prefer FETCH FIRST for top-N queries.
keywords.syntax: WHERE ROWNUM <= 10

keywords.name: ROWID
keywords.doc: Pseudocolumn holding the physical address of a row; the fastest way to reach a single row.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ROWID, last_name FROM employees

keywords.name: ORA_ROWSCN
keywords.doc: Pseudocolumn giving the system change number (SCN) of the most recent change to the row's block (or row, with ROWDEPENDENCIES).

keywords.name: NEXTVAL
keywords.doc: Sequence pseudocolumn that increments the sequence and returns the new value.
keywords.syntax: sequence_name.NEXTVAL

keywords.name: CURRVAL
keywords.doc: Sequence pseudocolumn returning the value most recently given by NEXTVAL in this session.
keywords.syntax: sequence_name.CURRVAL

keywords.name: DUAL
keywords.doc: A one-row, one-column table owned by SYS, used to select expressions. From 23ai the FROM clause may be omitted instead.
keywords.syntax: SELECT SYSDATE FROM DUAL

keywords.name: MERGE
keywords.doc: Inserts, updates or deletes rows in a target table based on a join with a source (upsert).
keywords.syntax: MERGE INTO target USING source ON (condition) WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET ... WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT ...

keywords.name: MERGE INTO
keywords.doc: Starts a MERGE statement naming the target table.
keywords.syntax: MERGE INTO target t USING source s ON (t.id = s.id) ...

keywords.name: MATCHED
keywords.doc: Used in the WHEN MATCHED and WHEN NOT MATCHED branches of MERGE.

keywords.name: WHEN MATCHED
keywords.doc: MERGE branch for source rows that match a target row; usually UPDATE SET ..., optionally with WHERE and DELETE WHERE.
keywords.syntax: WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET col = expr [WHERE ...] [DELETE WHERE ...]

keywords.name: WHEN NOT MATCHED
keywords.doc: MERGE branch for source rows with no matching target row; usually INSERT.
keywords.syntax: WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN INSERT (cols) VALUES (exprs) [WHERE ...]

keywords.name: PIVOT
keywords.doc: Rotates rows into columns, aggregating values for each listed value of a column.
keywords.syntax: PIVOT (aggregate(expr) FOR column IN (value [AS alias], ...))

keywords.name: UNPIVOT
keywords.doc: Rotates columns into rows.
keywords.syntax: UNPIVOT [INCLUDE | EXCLUDE NULLS] (value_col FOR name_col IN (col [AS literal], ...))

keywords.name: MODEL
keywords.doc: Treats query results as a multidimensional array and computes cells with spreadsheet-like rules.
keywords.syntax: MODEL [PARTITION BY (...)] DIMENSION BY (...) MEASURES (...) RULES (...)

keywords.name: DIMENSION BY
keywords.doc: In a MODEL clause, lists the columns that identify a cell within a partition.
keywords.syntax: DIMENSION BY (col, ...)

keywords.name: MEASURES
keywords.doc: In a MODEL clause, lists the cell values the rules can read and assign; also used in MATCH_RECOGNIZE.
keywords.syntax: MEASURES (expr [AS alias], ...)

keywords.name: RULES
keywords.doc: In a MODEL clause, the cell assignments to compute.
keywords.syntax: RULES [UPSERT | UPDATE] [AUTOMATIC | SEQUENTIAL ORDER] (cell = expr, ...)

keywords.name: ROLLUP
keywords.doc: GROUP BY extension that adds subtotal rows for each prefix of the listed columns and a grand total.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY ROLLUP (a, b)

keywords.name: CUBE
keywords.doc: GROUP BY extension that adds subtotal rows for every combination of the listed columns.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY CUBE (a, b)

keywords.name: GROUPING SETS
keywords.doc: GROUP BY extension that computes several groupings in one query.
keywords.syntax: GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((a, b), (a), ())

keywords.name: SEQUENCE
keywords.doc: A schema object that generates unique integers.
keywords.syntax: CREATE SEQUENCE name [START WITH n] [INCREMENT BY n] [CACHE n | NOCACHE] [CYCLE | NOCYCLE]

keywords.name: INCREMENT BY
keywords.doc: Sets the step between values of a sequence or identity column.
keywords.syntax: INCREMENT BY n

keywords.name: SYNONYM
keywords.doc: An alias for a table, view, sequence, procedure or other object.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR REPLACE] [PUBLIC] SYNONYM name FOR [schema.]object

keywords.name: PUBLIC
keywords.doc: Makes a synonym or database link available to all users, or grants a privilege to every user.

keywords.name: PACKAGE
keywords.doc: A PL/SQL unit grouping related types, variables, procedures and functions; the specification declares the public interface.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR REPLACE] PACKAGE name {IS | AS} declarations END [name];

keywords.name: PACKAGE BODY
keywords.doc: The implementation of a package's procedures and functions, plus its private declarations.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR REPLACE] PACKAGE BODY name {IS | AS} ... [BEGIN ...] END [name];

keywords.name: BODY
keywords.doc: Used in PACKAGE BODY and TYPE BODY.

keywords.name: PROCEDURE
keywords.doc: A named PL/SQL block that performs an action and can take IN, OUT and IN OUT parameters.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR REPLACE] PROCEDURE name [(params)] {IS | AS} declarations BEGIN ... END [name];

keywords.name: FUNCTION
keywords.doc: A named PL/SQL block that returns a value and can be called from SQL or PL/SQL.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION name [(params)] RETURN type {IS | AS} ... BEGIN ... RETURN expr; END [name];

keywords.name: RETURN
keywords.doc: Declares a function's return type, or in PL/SQL exits a subprogram, returning a value from a function.
keywords.syntax: RETURN type | RETURN [expr];

keywords.name: RETURNING
keywords.doc: Returns values from rows affected by INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or MERGE into variables; also sets the result type of JSON functions.
keywords.syntax: ... RETURNING expr, ... [BULK COLLECT] INTO variables

keywords.name: DECLARE
keywords.doc: Starts the declaration section of an anonymous PL/SQL block.
keywords.syntax: DECLARE declarations BEGIN statements [EXCEPTION handlers] END;

keywords.name: EXCEPTION
keywords.doc: Starts the exception-handling section of a PL/SQL block, or declares a user-defined exception.
keywords.syntax: EXCEPTION WHEN exception_name THEN statements | name EXCEPTION;

keywords.name: WHEN OTHERS
keywords.doc: PL/SQL exception handler that catches every exception not handled earlier in the block.
keywords.syntax: EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN statements

keywords.name: OTHERS
keywords.doc: Used in WHEN OTHERS exception handlers.

keywords.name: RAISE
keywords.doc: Raises a named exception, or re-raises the current one inside an exception handler.
keywords.syntax: RAISE [exception_name];

keywords.name: PRAGMA
keywords.doc: A compiler directive in PL/SQL.
keywords.syntax: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION | EXCEPTION_INIT(name, -n) | SERIALLY_REUSABLE | UDF ...;

keywords.name: AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION
keywords.doc: Pragma that runs a subprogram in its own independent transaction, which it must commit or roll back.
keywords.syntax: PRAGMA AUTONOMOUS_TRANSACTION;

keywords.name: EXCEPTION_INIT
keywords.doc: Pragma that associates a user-defined exception with an Oracle error number.
keywords.syntax: PRAGMA EXCEPTION_INIT(exception_name, -error_number);

keywords.name: LOOP
keywords.doc: Starts a PL/SQL loop, ended by END LOOP.
keywords.syntax: [WHILE condition | FOR i IN [REVERSE] a..b] LOOP statements END LOOP;

keywords.name: END LOOP
keywords.doc: Ends a PL/SQL LOOP, WHILE LOOP or FOR LOOP.

keywords.name: END IF
keywords.doc: Ends a PL/SQL IF statement.

keywords.name: FOR
keywords.doc: Starts a PL/SQL FOR loop; also used in FOR UPDATE, PIVOT ... FOR, and CREATE SYNONYM ... FOR.
keywords.syntax: FOR i IN [REVERSE] lower..upper LOOP ... END LOOP;

keywords.name: WHILE
keywords.doc: Starts a PL/SQL loop that runs while a condition is true.
keywords.syntax: WHILE condition LOOP statements END LOOP;

keywords.name: EXIT
keywords.doc: Leaves the current PL/SQL loop, optionally only when a condition holds.
keywords.syntax: EXIT [label] [WHEN condition];

keywords.name: EXIT WHEN
keywords.doc: Leaves the current PL/SQL loop when a condition is true.
keywords.syntax: EXIT WHEN cursor%NOTFOUND;

keywords.name: CONTINUE
keywords.doc: Skips to the next iteration of the current PL/SQL loop.
keywords.syntax: CONTINUE [label] [WHEN condition];

keywords.name: IF
keywords.doc: PL/SQL conditional statement. In 23ai DDL, IF EXISTS / IF NOT EXISTS make CREATE and DROP skip silently.
keywords.syntax: IF condition THEN ... [ELSIF condition THEN ...] [ELSE ...] END IF; | DROP TABLE IF EXISTS t

keywords.name: ELSIF
keywords.doc: PL/SQL else-if branch of an IF statement (note the spelling).
keywords.syntax: ELSIF condition THEN statements

keywords.name: GOTO
keywords.doc: Transfers control in PL/SQL to a labeled statement.
keywords.syntax: GOTO label;

keywords.name: CURSOR
keywords.doc: Declares a named PL/SQL cursor for a query; REF CURSOR declares a cursor variable type.
keywords.syntax: CURSOR name [(params)] IS select_statement;

keywords.name: OPEN
keywords.doc: Opens a PL/SQL cursor, running its query; OPEN ... FOR opens a cursor variable.
keywords.syntax: OPEN cursor [(args)]; | OPEN cursor_var FOR query;

keywords.name: CLOSE
keywords.doc: Closes a PL/SQL cursor and releases its resources.
keywords.syntax: CLOSE cursor;

keywords.name: BULK COLLECT
keywords.doc: Fetches many rows at once into PL/SQL collections.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ... BULK COLLECT INTO collection | FETCH c BULK COLLECT INTO coll [LIMIT n]

keywords.name: BULK
keywords.doc: Used in BULK COLLECT.

keywords.name: FORALL
keywords.doc: Runs one DML statement for many collection elements in a single round trip.
keywords.syntax: FORALL i IN coll.FIRST..coll.LAST [SAVE EXCEPTIONS] dml_statement;

keywords.name: TYPE
keywords.doc: Declares a PL/SQL type (record, collection, REF CURSOR) or a schema object type. %TYPE takes the type of a column or variable.
keywords.syntax: TYPE name IS RECORD (...) | TABLE OF type [INDEX BY ...] | VARRAY(n) OF type | REF CURSOR

keywords.name: SUBTYPE
keywords.doc: Declares a PL/SQL subtype of a base type, optionally constrained.
keywords.syntax: SUBTYPE name IS base_type [(constraint)] [NOT NULL];

keywords.name: RECORD
keywords.doc: A PL/SQL composite type with named fields.
keywords.syntax: TYPE name IS RECORD (field type [, ...]);

keywords.name: ROWTYPE
keywords.doc: Used as %ROWTYPE to declare a record matching a table's or cursor's row.
keywords.syntax: variable table_name%ROWTYPE;

keywords.name: VARRAY
keywords.doc: A PL/SQL or schema collection type with a maximum size and ordered elements.
keywords.syntax: TYPE name IS VARRAY(n) OF element_type;

keywords.name: INDEX BY
keywords.doc: Makes a PL/SQL TABLE OF type an associative array keyed by integer or string.
keywords.syntax: TYPE name IS TABLE OF type INDEX BY PLS_INTEGER | VARCHAR2(n);

keywords.name: OBJECT
keywords.doc: Declares a schema object type with attributes and methods.
keywords.syntax: CREATE [OR REPLACE] TYPE name AS OBJECT (attr type, ...);

keywords.name: CONSTANT
keywords.doc: Declares a PL/SQL constant, which must be initialized and cannot change.
keywords.syntax: name CONSTANT type := value;

keywords.name: EXECUTE
keywords.doc: Runs dynamic SQL (EXECUTE IMMEDIATE) or grants the right to run a program unit (GRANT EXECUTE).

keywords.name: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE
keywords.doc: Runs a dynamic SQL statement or anonymous PL/SQL block built at run time.
keywords.syntax: EXECUTE IMMEDIATE sql_string [INTO vars] [USING binds] [RETURNING INTO vars];

keywords.name: IMMEDIATE
keywords.doc: Used in EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, and SHUTDOWN or constraint checking options.

keywords.name: OR REPLACE
keywords.doc: Replaces an existing object of the same name instead of failing.
keywords.syntax: CREATE OR REPLACE { VIEW | PROCEDURE | FUNCTION | PACKAGE | TRIGGER | TYPE | SYNONYM } ...

keywords.name: GRANT
keywords.doc: Gives system privileges, object privileges or roles to users or roles.
keywords.syntax: GRANT privilege [, ...] [ON object] TO grantee [WITH GRANT OPTION | WITH ADMIN OPTION]

keywords.name: REVOKE
keywords.doc: Removes privileges or roles from users or roles.
keywords.syntax: REVOKE privilege [, ...] [ON object] FROM grantee

keywords.name: TO
keywords.doc: Used in GRANT ... TO, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, RENAME ... TO, and interval types such as DAY TO SECOND.

keywords.name: TRUNCATE
keywords.doc: Removes all rows from a table quickly, without firing DELETE triggers; it is DDL and commits implicitly.
keywords.syntax: TRUNCATE TABLE name [DROP | REUSE STORAGE] [CASCADE]

keywords.name: PURGE
keywords.doc: Permanently removes a dropped object from the recycle bin, or drops a table without keeping it there.
keywords.syntax: DROP TABLE name PURGE | PURGE { TABLE name | RECYCLEBIN | DBA_RECYCLEBIN }

keywords.name: FLASHBACK
keywords.doc: Restores a table to an earlier point in time, or recovers a dropped table from the recycle bin.
keywords.syntax: FLASHBACK TABLE name TO { TIMESTAMP expr | SCN n | BEFORE DROP [RENAME TO new_name] }

keywords.name: AS OF
keywords.doc: Flashback query: reads a table as it was at a past time or SCN.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ... FROM t AS OF TIMESTAMP (SYSTIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '10' MINUTE)

keywords.name: COMMENT
keywords.doc: Adds a comment to a table, view, materialized view or column in the data dictionary.
keywords.syntax: COMMENT ON { TABLE t | COLUMN t.c } IS 'text'

keywords.name: RENAME
keywords.doc: Renames a table, view, sequence or synonym, or (with ALTER TABLE) a column or constraint.
keywords.syntax: RENAME old_name TO new_name

keywords.name: MODIFY
keywords.doc: In ALTER TABLE, changes a column's type, default, nullability or visibility, or a constraint's state.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t MODIFY (col type [DEFAULT expr])

keywords.name: CASCADE
keywords.doc: Also drops or affects dependent objects, such as referencing constraints.
keywords.syntax: DROP TABLE t CASCADE CONSTRAINTS | DROP USER u CASCADE

keywords.name: ENABLE
keywords.doc: Turns on a constraint, trigger or feature.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t ENABLE CONSTRAINT name

keywords.name: DISABLE
keywords.doc: Turns off a constraint, trigger or feature.
keywords.syntax: ALTER TABLE t DISABLE CONSTRAINT name

keywords.name: NOCOPY
keywords.doc: Hint that an OUT or IN OUT parameter should be passed by reference to avoid copying large values.
keywords.syntax: param IN OUT NOCOPY type

keywords.name: IN OUT
keywords.doc: PL/SQL parameter mode: the value is passed in and changes are passed back to the caller.
keywords.syntax: name IN OUT [NOCOPY] type

keywords.name: OUT
keywords.doc: PL/SQL parameter mode: the subprogram assigns a value that is returned to the caller.
keywords.syntax: name OUT [NOCOPY] type

keywords.name: AUTHID
keywords.doc: Sets whether a PL/SQL unit runs with the privileges of its owner (DEFINER, the default) or its caller (CURRENT_USER).
keywords.syntax: AUTHID { CURRENT_USER | DEFINER }

keywords.name: DEFINER
keywords.doc: Used in AUTHID DEFINER: the unit runs with its owner's privileges.

keywords.name: DETERMINISTIC
keywords.doc: Declares that a function always returns the same result for the same arguments, allowing caching and use in function-based indexes.
keywords.syntax: FUNCTION f (...) RETURN type DETERMINISTIC IS ...

keywords.name: PIPELINED
keywords.doc: Declares a table function that returns rows one at a time with PIPE ROW, for use in FROM TABLE(...).
keywords.syntax: FUNCTION f RETURN collection_type PIPELINED IS ... PIPE ROW (value); ... RETURN;

keywords.name: PIPE ROW
keywords.doc: Returns one row from a pipelined table function.
keywords.syntax: PIPE ROW (value);

keywords.name: PARALLEL_ENABLE
keywords.doc: Declares that a function can be run safely by parallel query servers.
keywords.syntax: FUNCTION f (...) RETURN type PARALLEL_ENABLE IS ...

keywords.name: RESULT_CACHE
keywords.doc: Caches a function's results across sessions, reusing them for the same arguments.
keywords.syntax: FUNCTION f (...) RETURN type RESULT_CACHE IS ...

keywords.name: NULLS FIRST
keywords.doc: Sorts NULLs before non-NULL values (the default for DESC).
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY expr [ASC | DESC] NULLS FIRST

keywords.name: NULLS LAST
keywords.doc: Sorts NULLs after non-NULL values (the default for ASC).
keywords.syntax: ORDER BY expr [ASC | DESC] NULLS LAST

keywords.name: NULLS
keywords.doc: Used in NULLS FIRST, NULLS LAST, IGNORE NULLS, RESPECT NULLS and UNPIVOT INCLUDE NULLS.

keywords.name: IGNORE NULLS
keywords.doc: Makes FIRST_VALUE, LAST_VALUE, NTH_VALUE, LAG or LEAD skip NULL values.
keywords.syntax: LAG(expr) IGNORE NULLS OVER (...)

keywords.name: RESPECT NULLS
keywords.doc: Makes analytic functions consider NULL values (the default).
keywords.syntax: FIRST_VALUE(expr) RESPECT NULLS OVER (...)

keywords.name: WITHIN GROUP
keywords.doc: Supplies the ordering for LISTAGG, PERCENTILE_CONT, PERCENTILE_DISC and hypothetical-set aggregates.
keywords.syntax: LISTAGG(expr, ',') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY expr)

keywords.name: WITHIN
keywords.doc: Used in WITHIN GROUP.

keywords.name: KEEP
keywords.doc: With an aggregate, computes it only over the rows that rank first or last by an ordering.
keywords.syntax: MAX(salary) KEEP (DENSE_RANK FIRST ORDER BY hire_date)

keywords.name: LATERAL
keywords.doc: Lets an inline view in FROM refer to columns of tables to its left.
keywords.syntax: FROM t, LATERAL (SELECT ... WHERE x = t.x) v

keywords.name: APPLY
keywords.doc: Used in CROSS APPLY and OUTER APPLY.

keywords.name: CROSS APPLY
keywords.doc: Joins each left row to the rows produced by a correlated table expression; left rows with no result are dropped.
keywords.syntax: FROM t CROSS APPLY (SELECT ... WHERE x = t.x) v

keywords.name: OUTER APPLY
keywords.doc: Like CROSS APPLY, but keeps left rows with no result, filling NULLs.
keywords.syntax: FROM t OUTER APPLY (SELECT ... WHERE x = t.x) v

keywords.name: FOR UPDATE
keywords.doc: Locks the selected rows until the transaction ends.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE [OF col, ...] [NOWAIT | WAIT n | SKIP LOCKED]

keywords.name: NOWAIT
keywords.doc: Fails immediately instead of waiting when a row or table is already locked.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE NOWAIT

keywords.name: WAIT
keywords.doc: Waits up to n seconds for a lock before failing.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE WAIT n

keywords.name: SKIP LOCKED
keywords.doc: Skips rows already locked by other sessions instead of waiting, as in job-queue patterns.
keywords.syntax: SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED

keywords.name: LOCK TABLE
keywords.doc: Locks a table in a given mode until the transaction ends.
keywords.syntax: LOCK TABLE t IN { SHARE | EXCLUSIVE | ROW EXCLUSIVE ... } MODE [NOWAIT | WAIT n]

keywords.name: GLOBAL TEMPORARY
keywords.doc: Creates a table whose definition is permanent but whose rows are private to each session or transaction.
keywords.syntax: CREATE GLOBAL TEMPORARY TABLE t (...) ON COMMIT { DELETE | PRESERVE } ROWS

keywords.name: GLOBAL
keywords.doc: Used in GLOBAL TEMPORARY tables and global partitioned indexes.

keywords.name: PRIVATE TEMPORARY
keywords.doc: Creates a temporary table (named with the ORA$PTT_ prefix by default) that exists only in memory for the session or transaction. (Oracle 18c+)
keywords.syntax: CREATE PRIVATE TEMPORARY TABLE ora$ptt_t (...) ON COMMIT { DROP | PRESERVE } DEFINITION

keywords.name: TEMPORARY
keywords.doc: Used in GLOBAL TEMPORARY and PRIVATE TEMPORARY tables and temporary tablespaces.

keywords.name: PRESERVE
keywords.doc: Keeps temporary table rows (ON COMMIT PRESERVE ROWS) or a private temporary table (ON COMMIT PRESERVE DEFINITION) after commit.

keywords.name: IDENTITY
keywords.doc: An auto-generated numeric column backed by an internal sequence.
keywords.syntax: col NUMBER GENERATED { ALWAYS | BY DEFAULT [ON NULL] } AS IDENTITY [(START WITH n INCREMENT BY n)]

keywords.name: GENERATED
keywords.doc: Used in identity columns and virtual columns.
keywords.syntax: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY | GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr) VIRTUAL

keywords.name: ALWAYS
keywords.doc: In an identity column, the value is always generated and cannot be supplied.
keywords.syntax: GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY

keywords.name: INVISIBLE
keywords.doc: Hides a column from SELECT * and positional INSERT, or makes an index ignored by the optimizer.
keywords.syntax: col type INVISIBLE | ALTER INDEX i INVISIBLE

keywords.name: VISIBLE
keywords.doc: Makes an invisible column or index visible again.

keywords.name: VIRTUAL
keywords.doc: A column whose value is computed from an expression and not stored.
keywords.syntax: col [type] [GENERATED ALWAYS] AS (expr) [VIRTUAL]

keywords.name: TABLESPACE
keywords.doc: A logical storage container of data files; tables and indexes are stored in one.
keywords.syntax: CREATE TABLE t (...) TABLESPACE users

keywords.name: SCHEMA
keywords.doc: The collection of objects owned by a user; ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA changes name resolution.
keywords.syntax: ALTER SESSION SET CURRENT_SCHEMA = name

keywords.name: SESSION
keywords.doc: Used in ALTER SESSION to change settings for the current session.
keywords.syntax: ALTER SESSION SET parameter = value

keywords.name: ROLE
keywords.doc: A named set of privileges that can be granted to users or other roles.
keywords.syntax: CREATE ROLE name | SET ROLE name

keywords.name: MATERIALIZED VIEW
keywords.doc: A view whose query result is stored and can be refreshed, fully or incrementally.
keywords.syntax: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW name [BUILD IMMEDIATE] [REFRESH { FAST | COMPLETE | FORCE } ON { COMMIT | DEMAND }] AS query

keywords.name: MATERIALIZED
keywords.doc: Used in MATERIALIZED VIEW.

keywords.name: DOMAIN
keywords.doc: A reusable data-use definition (type, constraints, display and ordering expressions) applied to columns. (Oracle 23ai+)
keywords.syntax: CREATE DOMAIN name AS type [CONSTRAINT ...] | col type DOMAIN name

keywords.name: IS JSON
keywords.doc: Condition that is true when a value is well-formed JSON, optionally of a given kind.
keywords.syntax: expr IS [NOT] JSON [VALUE | SCALAR | OBJECT | ARRAY] [STRICT | LAX] [WITH UNIQUE KEYS]

keywords.name: ORDINALITY
keywords.doc: In JSON_TABLE or XMLTABLE, a column that numbers the generated rows.
keywords.syntax: col FOR ORDINALITY

keywords.name: NESTED PATH
keywords.doc: In JSON_TABLE, unnests a nested array into additional rows.
keywords.syntax: NESTED PATH '$.items[*]' COLUMNS (...)

keywords.name: PATH
keywords.doc: In JSON_TABLE or XMLTABLE, the path that locates a column's value.
keywords.syntax: col type PATH '$.field'

keywords.name: COLUMNS
keywords.doc: In JSON_TABLE or XMLTABLE, starts the list of output column definitions.

keywords.name: PASSING
keywords.doc: Binds SQL values to variables in XQuery or SQL/JSON path expressions.
keywords.syntax: PASSING expr AS "name"

keywords.name: MATCH_RECOGNIZE
keywords.doc: Finds patterns of rows (row pattern matching) using a regular-expression-like PATTERN over ordered data.
keywords.syntax: MATCH_RECOGNIZE (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ... MEASURES ... PATTERN (...) DEFINE ...)

keywords.name: SEARCH
keywords.doc: In a recursive WITH clause, orders rows depth-first or breadth-first.
keywords.syntax: SEARCH { DEPTH | BREADTH } FIRST BY col SET order_col

keywords.name: CYCLE
keywords.doc: In a recursive WITH clause marks cycles; in a sequence, restarts after the maximum value.
keywords.syntax: CYCLE col SET is_cycle TO 'Y' DEFAULT 'N'

keywords.name: NOCACHE
keywords.doc: Sequence or table option that disables caching of values or blocks.

constants.name: TRUE
constants.doc: The BOOLEAN true value. (BOOLEAN is a SQL type from Oracle 23ai; always available in PL/SQL.)

constants.name: FALSE
constants.doc: The BOOLEAN false value. (BOOLEAN is a SQL type from Oracle 23ai; always available in PL/SQL.)

types.name: NUMBER
types.doc: Exact decimal number with up to 38 digits of precision. Without arguments it stores any value in range; NUMBER(p, s) fixes precision and scale.

types.name: INTEGER
types.doc: ANSI synonym for NUMBER(38), an integer with up to 38 digits.

types.name: INT
types.doc: ANSI synonym for NUMBER(38).

types.name: SMALLINT
types.doc: ANSI synonym for NUMBER(38); Oracle does not store it in fewer bytes.

types.name: NUMERIC
types.doc: ANSI synonym for NUMBER(p, s).

types.name: DECIMAL
types.doc: ANSI synonym for NUMBER(p, s).

types.name: DEC
types.doc: ANSI synonym for NUMBER(p, s).

types.name: FLOAT
types.doc: A NUMBER subtype with binary precision (1 to 126 bits, default 126); still a decimal type, unlike BINARY_DOUBLE.

types.name: REAL
types.doc: ANSI type mapped to FLOAT(63).

types.name: DOUBLE
types.doc: DOUBLE PRECISION is an ANSI type mapped to FLOAT(126).

types.name: BINARY_FLOAT
types.doc: 32-bit IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point number; supports NaN and infinity.

types.name: BINARY_DOUBLE
types.doc: 64-bit IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point number; supports NaN and infinity.

types.name: VARCHAR2
types.doc: Variable-length text in the database character set, up to 4000 bytes, or 32767 with MAX_STRING_SIZE = EXTENDED. Length may be in BYTE or CHAR.

types.name: NVARCHAR2
types.doc: Variable-length Unicode text in the national character set, with length in characters.

types.name: VARCHAR
types.doc: Currently a synonym of VARCHAR2; Oracle recommends VARCHAR2 because VARCHAR semantics may change.

types.name: CHAR
types.doc: Fixed-length text, blank-padded to its length (default 1), up to 2000 bytes.

types.name: CHARACTER
types.doc: ANSI synonym for CHAR; CHARACTER VARYING is a synonym for VARCHAR2.

types.name: NCHAR
types.doc: Fixed-length Unicode text in the national character set, with length in characters.

types.name: CLOB
types.doc: Character large object for text up to (4 GB - 1) * block size, in the database character set.

types.name: NCLOB
types.doc: Character large object in the national character set.

types.name: BLOB
types.doc: Binary large object for unstructured binary data up to (4 GB - 1) * block size.

types.name: BFILE
types.doc: Locator for a binary file stored outside the database in an operating-system directory; read-only.

types.name: LONG
types.doc: Legacy variable-length text up to 2 GB; LONG RAW is its binary form. Deprecated: use CLOB or BLOB.

types.name: RAW
types.doc: Variable-length binary data up to 2000 bytes, or 32767 with MAX_STRING_SIZE = EXTENDED.

types.name: DATE
types.doc: Date and time to the second (century, year, month, day, hour, minute, second), with no fractional seconds or time zone.

types.name: TIMESTAMP
types.doc: Date and time with fractional seconds (0 to 9 digits, default 6). WITH TIME ZONE stores an offset or region; WITH LOCAL TIME ZONE normalizes to the database zone and shows in the session zone.

types.name: INTERVAL
types.doc: A span of time: YEAR TO MONTH for years and months, or DAY TO SECOND for days, hours, minutes and seconds.
types.syntax: INTERVAL YEAR[(yp)] TO MONTH | INTERVAL DAY[(dp)] TO SECOND[(fsp)]

types.name: BOOLEAN
types.doc: TRUE, FALSE or NULL. A SQL column type from Oracle 23ai; always available in PL/SQL.

types.name: JSON
types.doc: Native binary JSON (OSON) type for documents, arrays and scalars. (Oracle 21c+)

types.name: XMLTYPE
types.doc: Stores XML documents, with methods and SQL/XML functions to query them.

types.name: ROWID
types.doc: The physical address of a row in its base-64 extended format; also the ROWID pseudocolumn.

types.name: UROWID
types.doc: Universal rowid: the logical or physical address of a row, including rows of index-organized and foreign tables.

types.name: PLS_INTEGER
types.doc: PL/SQL signed 32-bit integer using native machine arithmetic; faster than NUMBER. PL/SQL only.

types.name: BINARY_INTEGER
types.doc: PL/SQL synonym of PLS_INTEGER. PL/SQL only.

types.name: SIMPLE_INTEGER
types.doc: PL/SQL subtype of PLS_INTEGER that is NOT NULL and wraps on overflow instead of raising an error. PL/SQL only.

types.name: SYS_REFCURSOR
types.doc: Predefined weak REF CURSOR type for passing query result sets between PL/SQL units and to clients.

types.name: SDO_GEOMETRY
types.doc: Oracle Spatial object type for points, lines, polygons and collections, with a coordinate system (SRID).

types.name: VECTOR
types.doc: Vector of numbers for AI similarity search; dimension count and element format (INT8, FLOAT32, FLOAT64, BINARY) may be fixed or * for any. (Oracle 23ai+)
